item.title: Denosumab biosimilars summarised in new MIMS table
item.description: A comparison table of denosumab preparations is now available to MIMS subscribers, following a recent wave of biosimilar launches.

item.title: 'Profound perception change​' in ​gout management​​ called for, as treating​-to​-target linked to fewer cardiovascular events
item.description: Gout patients who achieved a serum urate level of less than 6mg/dL with urate-lowering treatment had a lower risk of major adverse cardiovascular events than those who did not, according to a new study.

item.title: ‘Breakthrough’ COPD treatment approved for NHS use
item.description: Dupilumab has been recommended as an add-on maintenance treatment option for adults with uncontrolled COPD and raised blood eosinophils, in final draft NICE guidance.

item.title: Statin prescribing information updated to highlight that most reported muscle symptoms not caused by the drugs
item.description: Product information for statins is being updated to reflect the fact that less than 10% of reported muscle-related adverse events are attributable to the medication.

item.title: Pancreatitis warnings strengthened for GLP-1 drugs
item.description: Increased vigilance is needed for rare but potentially fatal pancreatitis in patients taking GLP-1 drugs for diabetes or weight loss, the MHRA says.

item.title: RSV vaccination to be offered to 3 million more older adults
item.description: An additional 3 million older adults will be eligible to receive the RSV vaccine on the NHS from April, as the vaccination programme is extended to over-80s.

item.title: Dormant medicine licences to be revived in bid to tackle critical drug shortages
item.description: Dormant medicine licences will be reactivated under a plan to tackle drug shortages through a new partnership between NHS England, the MHRA, and the pharmaceutical industry.

item.title: Medicines shortages 'a national security risk', warn Lords
item.description: In an era of rising geopolitical tension, medicine supply should be treated as a national security issue, according to a new House of Lords report.

item.title: Semaglutide prescribing information to highlight rare vision loss risk
item.description: Yellow Card reports have prompted updated advice on the risk of nonarteritic anterior ischaemic optic neuropathy (NAION) in patients using semaglutide.

item.title: UKMEC update: practices may need to review patients’ contraception, says GP
item.description: Practices will need to review some patients’ contraceptive prescriptions to ensure compliance with the recently updated UK Medical Eligibility Criteria for Contraceptive Use, GP Dr Toni Hazell says in the MIMS Learning Clinical Update podcast.
